SMTO-AUT-0028 — Google didn't give SMTO usable access

GUID: 2d925123-c630-5abb-b186-40fe7b905923
Slug: google-not-authorized
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • Google's reply didn't include access SMTO could accept, so your Google account wasn't connected or renewed this time. SMTO saved nothing from the reply, and the request that needed Google didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to connect the same Google account again, and on Google's page approve all the access it lists. Google only returns usable access when the sign-in is completed and approved.
  2. Sign in with the same Google email address that SMTO already has saved for this account. Using the intended account keeps SMTO from connecting or acting as someone else.
  3. If Google rejects it again, ask the person who manages SMTO to check that the Google Workspace OAuth App entry's client ID and secret match the app in Google Cloud. If the app's secret was reset or deleted at Google, every sign-in and renewal fails until the entry is updated.

What success looks like

  • The Google sign-in page says your email is connected, and your request runs without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the Google client secret, sign-in codes or anything from the browser's address bar into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google token validation rejected the code exchange or refresh result: an empty authorization code, a malformed or missing token field, no granted-scope list on first consent, an out-of-range expiry, or a provider error other than invalid_grant.

What this means

  • Google token-bundle validation rejected missing/malformed token fields, absent initial scope evidence or a provider authorization error. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Google token-bundle validation rejected missing/malformed token fields, absent initial scope evidence or a provider authorization error.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the token-validation stage and public consent status; check application configuration without exposing the rejected token response.

How to fix it

  • Check the google_oauth_app client_id and client_secret against the app in Google Cloud Console (an invalid_client response maps here), confirm the consent returned a code and a scope list, then reconnect the intended account with auth.google_connect. token_bundle requires a Bearer access_token, a positive expires_in under ten years and, on first consent, an explicit scope field.
  • Reconnect the intended account and approve the requested features. Check application configuration if Google rejects consent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended authorization yields a validated token bundle and recorded provider-granted scopes.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
